before.content:
<!-- layout: title; theme: keynote; design: v1 -->
# The intake pilot

A shorter review cycle, with an unanswered quality question. [1][2]

---

<!-- layout: composed -->
<!-- scene:  -->
## The pilot measured time; quality remains unknown [1][2]

In this synthetic intake pilot, median review time was 40 hours before the pilot and 16 hours during the pilot. The observation covered two teams over eight weeks. These are training data, not actual organizational results. [1]

The two-team intake pilot did not measure review quality or error rates. A faster review cannot establish a quality improvement. The sample does not establish an effect in other teams. [2]

beforeFindings.problem: Body text is 17.8px; the body floor is 22px.
beforeFindings.correction: Allocate more room and increase type; keep values and qualifications intact.

beforeFindings.problem: The qualification paragraph — “did not measure review quality or error rates… the sample does not establish…” — is set at 17.75px, below the 22px minimum, and is squeezed into two very long lines at the top right while the rest of that half of the slide is empty. The content that limits the headline’s claim is the least legible text on the slide.
beforeFindings.correction: Set this block at the same body size as the left column (at least 22px) and give it a readable measure, using the available right-hand space rather than one wide, tiny paragraph. The limitation should read with equal visual weight to the time result.

beforeFindings.problem: The time result is forced into a roughly 204px-wide column, producing 15 very short lines. The extremely narrow measure makes the core result slow to scan and leaves the composition heavily unbalanced.
beforeFindings.correction: Widen the result column to a more readable measure, or reflow the slide into a balanced two-column layout so the result and the limitation use the space evenly.
